title.purpose: The page's h1 and every card's headline USD price — the single top type tier in the system, shared rather than separated into a larger display size.

body.purpose: Page subtitle, button labels, filter input text.

label.purpose: Coin symbols, badge text, small captions like the delta chip's "recent" caption.

mono.purpose: The BTC sub-price value only — fixed-width digits for scanability down a column of cards.

shadows.name: card-rest
shadows.purpose: Card's resting elevation — barely visible, the system's quietest shadow.

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Card's only elevation change, on hover — signals the card is liftable/draggable. No other component in the system ever uses a shadow.

motion.name: card-shadow-transition
motion.purpose: Smooths the rest-to-hover shadow step on cards. Gated behind motion-safe: — spatial-adjacent enough to skip under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: drag-transform
motion.purpose: Card position animates during drag-and-drop reorder. The transition string is dropped entirely under reduced motion — the drop still lands correctly, just instantly instead of sliding.

motion.name: refresh-spin
motion.purpose: RefreshCw icon spins while a refresh is in flight. Gated behind motion-safe: since the "Refreshing…" label already carries the state without it.

motion.name: badge-color-transition
motion.purpose: Staleness badge's tier color change. Deliberately NOT gated by motion-safe: — a color transition isn't the spatial movement reduced motion asks apps to remove.

motion.name: focus-ring
motion.purpose: focus-visible outline appears/disappears immediately — a focus indicator that faded in would be slower to notice, not more polished.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The only button style in the system — an outline/ghost control used for Refresh and other labeled actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #374151; border: 1px solid #d1d5db; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 6px 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 400; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #f9fafb; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #111827; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-ghost:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: Icon-only control used for the theme toggle.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-icon" aria-label="Toggle theme"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path d="M12 3a6 6 0 0 0 9 9 9 9 0 1 1-9-9Z"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-icon { background: transparent; color: #4b5563; border: 1px solid #d1d5db; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 8px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; } .ds-btn-icon:hover { background: #f9fafb; } .ds-btn-icon:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #111827; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-icon:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Drag Handle
components.description: Icon-only grab affordance on each card, borderless at rest. Padding was grown from 4px to 10px (24x24 -> 36x36 hit area) after an accessibility audit found it under the practical 44x44 touch-target minimum for the app's sole drag-and-drop grab point.
components.html: <button class="ds-drag-handle" aria-label="Reorder Bitcoin"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><circle cx="9" cy="6" r="1"/><circle cx="9" cy="12" r="1"/><circle cx="9" cy="18" r="1"/><circle cx="15" cy="6" r="1"/><circle cx="15" cy="12" r="1"/><circle cx="15" cy="18" r="1"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-drag-handle { background: transparent; color: #9ca3af; border: none; border-radius: 0.25rem; padding: 10px; touch-action: none; } .ds-drag-handle:hover { background: #f3f4f6; color: #4b5563; } .ds-drag-handle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #111827; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius: 0.75rem; padding: 16px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); } .ds-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 2px 4px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-card { transition: box-shadow 150ms ease; } } .ds-card-header { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; margin-bottom: 16px; } .ds-card-logo { width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #f3f4f6; } .ds-card-name { font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 600; color: #111827; line-height: 1.3; margin: 0; } .ds-card-symbol { font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; color: #6b7280; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-card-price { font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 600; color: #111827; } .ds-card-btc { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #6b7280; margin-top: 2px; }

components.name: Staleness Badge (Live)
components.description: One of four fixed-color pill badges signaling data freshness; always paired with a solid dot so state is never color-alone. Delayed/Stale/Never swap only the bg/text token pair. The tier color change animates via a 200ms transition (kept under reduced motion — see extensions.motion).
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 4px 10px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; transition: background-color 200ms, color 200ms; } .ds-badge-live { background: #dcfce7; color: #166534; } .ds-badge-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: currentColor; }

components.name: Filter Input
components.description: The page's single text filter, with a leading search icon.
components.css: .ds-input-wrap { position: relative; max-width: 20rem; } .ds-input-icon { position: absolute; left: 12px; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); color: #9ca3af; pointer-events: none; } .ds-input-filter { width: 100%; border: 1px solid #d1d5db; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 6px 12px 6px 36px; font-size: 0.875rem; color: #111827; } .ds-input-filter::placeholder { color: #9ca3af; } .ds-input-filter:focus { border-color: #9ca3af; } .ds-input-filter:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #111827; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Trend Sparkline
components.description: Signature component: a 64x24 inline SVG trend line, always muted, with only its final point colored by trend direction. Colors resolve from --status-good/--status-critical/--status-muted, which differ per theme (see colorMeta market-green-light/dark etc.) — this snippet shows the light-mode values.

narrative.overview:
This is a data-first dashboard, not a marketing surface: it reads like an instrument cluster built to be scanned at a glance, where the numbers are the interface and the chrome around them recedes on purpose. There is no brand accent color anywhere in the system — the entire UI is grayscale except for a small, fixed set of functional signal colors (market-green, market-red, neutral-gray, plus the amber/red/green badge pairs) that exist purely to carry state, never decoration. Every non-neutral pixel on screen is answering a question ("is this trending up?", "is this data fresh?") rather than expressing a personality.

Density stays comfortable rather than tight: cards get real breathing room (16px internal padding, 16px grid gutters), text sizes top out modestly (the largest text anywhere is 20px, on both the page title and each card's headline price — there is no oversized "hero" numeral), and the whole system rejects visual noise in favor of legibility at a glance. Nothing here was rejected from a louder direction; restraint was the starting brief, not a fallback.
keyCharacteristics: Fully grayscale base palette; color exists only as functional signal (trend direction, freshness state), never as brand or decoration.
Flat-by-default surfaces; the only shadow in the entire system is a single hover-elevation step on cards.
One typographic ceiling (20px/600) shared by the page title and every card's price — no oversized hero type.
Status is always color + a second cue (an icon, a label, or both) — color alone never carries meaning.
Coin logos are the one genuinely decorative element allowed; everything else is typographic or geometric.

rules.name: The No-Brand-Color Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this system is colored for decoration or identity. A color is only ever earned by carrying a state — trend direction or data freshness. If a future addition wants a "brand" color, that is a deliberate identity decision to make explicitly, not a default to reach for.

rules.name: The Static-Scan Rule
rules.body: Signal colors (Market Green/Red/Neutral Gray) must be applied via inline style (or CSS variables), never as a Tailwind arbitrary-value class built from a JS constant — Tailwind's static source scanner cannot see a template-literal class name at build time and will silently drop it. This was a real bug in this codebase; the fix is the standing rule.

rules.name: The Per-Theme Signal Rule
rules.body: A signal color never gets one fixed hex shared by both themes. Each of the three signal colors is tuned independently for light and dark so it clears 4.5:1 against its own card surface — a value picked for one theme is not assumed to work in the other without checking.

rules.name: The One-Tier-Up Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the interface is allowed to out-rank a card's own price in size or weight — the page title and the price sit at the exact same visual weight on purpose, reinforcing that the data is the content, not the chrome around it.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Shadows exist solely as hover feedback on interactive cards. No other component — button, input, badge, header — ever gets a shadow, at rest or on hover; their separation comes from a border or a background shift instead.

rules.name: The Muted-Line Rule
rules.body: A trend sparkline's line is always the neutral/muted hue; only its terminal point ever takes the signal color. No sparkline line is ever colored by direction across its full length.

rules.name: The Visible-Focus Rule
rules.body: Every interactive control shows a 2px focus-visible outline in Ink Primary, 2px offset, on keyboard focus — never suppressed. A prior version shipped outline-none on the filter input with no replacement, a real WCAG 2.4.7 gap; this is now a standing invariant, not a per-component choice.

rules.name: The Reduced-Motion Carve-Out
rules.body: Spatial motion (shadow transitions, drag-settle transforms, the refresh spin) is skipped entirely under prefers-reduced-motion. Color and state transitions that carry meaning, like the staleness badge's tier color change, are kept — reduced motion removes movement, not all feedback.

dos: Do treat every color as a state signal, not decoration — before adding any new hue, ask what state it represents.
Do pair every status or trend color with a non-color cue (an icon, a visible label, or both) — color alone never carries meaning anywhere in this system.
Do keep the drag/trend/staleness signal colors flowing through a single shared source of truth (STATUS_COLOR in code) rather than redefining them per component, so they cannot drift apart.
Do apply signal colors via inline style/CSS variables, never a Tailwind class built from a runtime constant.
Do keep the page title and a card's headline price at the same type size and weight — neither should ever out-rank the other.
Do give every interactive control a visible :focus-visible outline.
Do judge each animation against prefers-reduced-motion individually: drop spatial movement, keep color/state transitions that carry meaning.
donts: Don't add a shadow to anything except a card, and only as hover feedback — not at rest, and not to any other component.
Don't introduce a brand/decorative accent color; every non-neutral pixel must be answering "what state is this."
Don't color a sparkline's full line by trend direction — only its end marker carries the signal color.
Don't add a filled/primary-style button; every button in this system is an outline/ghost control.
Don't raise any text above the 20px/600 "Title" tier without a deliberate, system-wide decision — there is no hero-text precedent to extend from.
Don't ship outline-none (or equivalent) on any focusable element without an equally visible replacement indicator — this has already regressed once.
Don't give a single signal color one fixed hex for both themes; verify each theme's contrast independently before reusing a value across light and dark.
